title: How Clinicians Think and What AI Can Learn From It
abstract: arXiv:2601.12547v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence increasingly builds high-dimensional representations of patients, yet every finite clinical model is an abstraction. The key question is not only how accurately a model predicts, but which distinctions need to be represented, at what resolution, for the decision at hand. We argue that purposive clinical AI should use decision-sufficient abstraction: model detail should be conditioned by the objective structure of the decision and limited by the evidence available to support that detail.   We further argue that this objective structure should often be ordinal-first. The primitive objects are objective-threshold propositions that may recur at progressively finer levels. For example, mortality below 10 percent may appear early and mortality below 5 percent later. translated_title: 临床医生如何思考以及人工智能能从中学到什么
translated_abstract: 临床人工智能日益构建患者的高维表示，然而每一个有限的临床模型都是一种抽象。关键问题不仅在于模型预测得有多准确，还在于针对当前的决策，哪些区分需要被表示、以何种分辨率来表示。我们认为，有目的性的临床人工智能应当采用“决策充分抽象”原则：模型细节应由决策的目标结构所决定，并受可用于支持该细节的证据所限制。我们进一步论证，这种目标结构通常应当是“序数优先”的。其基本对象是可以在逐渐更精细的层级上重复出现的客观阈值命题。例如，“死亡率低于10%”可能较早出现，而“死亡率低于5%”则稍后出现。我们形式化了有序阈值细化、一种集值决策关系以及阈值充分抽象。一个模型只需要足够的分辨率（摘要内容在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文借鉴临床医生的思维方式，提出临床AI应采用“决策充分抽象”原则，以序数优先的阈值命题来决定模型所需的细节层次和分辨率，而非单纯追求预测精度。
en_tdlr: Drawing on how clinicians think, this paper proposes that clinical AI should adopt "decision-sufficient abstraction" based on ordinal-first threshold propositions, where model detail is determined by the decision's objective structure and bounded by available evidence rather than pure predictive accuracy.
